summary: This note is a match-by-match table of the Second City derby, the football rivalry between Aston Villa and Birmingham City (listed as Small Heath in 1901). It records 12 meetings from 1887 to 2015 with the date, venue, home team, score, competition, round and, for some matches, attendance. The matches span the FA Cup, League Cup and Full Members Cup.
one_line: Table of 12 Aston Villa vs Birmingham City (Second City derby) matches from 1887 to 2015, with venues, scores and competitions.
key_facts: The first listed Second City derby match was played on 5 November 1887 at Wellington Road, with Aston Villa winning 4-0 in the FA Cup 2nd Round.
On 23 March 1901 Small Heath drew 0-0 with Aston Villa at Muntz Street in the FA Cup Quarter Final.
The FA Cup Quarter Final replay was played on 27 March 1901 at Villa Park, and Aston Villa won 1-0.
The first leg of the 1963 League Cup Final was played on 23 May 1963 at St Andrew's, with Birmingham City winning 3-1, attendance 31,850.
The second leg of the 1963 League Cup Final was played on 27 May 1963 at Villa Park, ending 0-0, attendance 37,921.
On 27 September 1988 Birmingham City beat Aston Villa 2-0 at St Andrew's in the League Cup 2nd Round first leg.
On 12 October 1988 Aston Villa beat Birmingham City 5-0 at Villa Park in the League Cup 2nd Round second leg.
On 9 November 1988 Aston Villa won 6-0 at Villa Park in the Full Members Cup 1st Round, attendance 8,324.
On 21 September 1993 Birmingham City beat Aston Villa 1-0 at St Andrew's in the League Cup 2nd Round first leg, attendance 27,815.
On 6 October 1993 Aston Villa won 1-0 at Villa Park in the League Cup 2nd Round second leg, attendance 35,856.
On 1 December 2010 Birmingham City won 2-1 at St Andrew's in the League Cup Quarter Final, attendance 27,679.
On 22 September 2015 Aston Villa won 1-0 at Villa Park in the League Cup 3rd Round, attendance 34,442.
